title: AWL Agri Business Ltd - 543458 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: AWL Agri Q4 FY26 revenue hit a record INR 21,000+ crore (+18% YoY) on 14% volume growth to ~1.9 MMT; EBITDA per ton ~INR 3,400.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 delivered record quarterly revenue, with volume up 14% to about 1.9 million tonnes and operational EBITDA of INR 628 crore (+40% YoY). Edible oil volume grew 17% and Food/FMCG about 6%, while Industry Essentials grew 13%. Management flagged that the March 2026 Iran conflict pushed crude-linked input costs (packaging, chemicals, coal) and edible oil prices higher, with the cost impact expected to hit Q1 FY27 rather than Q4. April demand was sluggish, with management expecting recovery in May and June.

segments.name: Edible Oil
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +17% YoY and revenue INR 17,520 crore (+19% YoY); FY26 volume +6%. Market share up 60 bps in Q4; e-com and quick commerce share held above 30%.

segments.name: Food and FMCG
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +6% (about +3% normalised for FY26 G2G exit); FY26 volume -4% reported, +3%+ normalised. Basmati rice share up 330 bps to near 9%; wheat flour share flat at 5.3-5.4%. Segment profit about INR 35 crore in Q4 and about INR 200 crore for FY26.

segments.name: Industry Essentials
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +13% and revenue +11% YoY; FY26 volume +8%. Oleo chemicals are about 30% of the segment; specialty chemicals about 7-8% of portfolio. New Krishnapatnam capacity expected by early Q4 FY27.

segments.name: GD Foods (subsidiary)
segments.commentary: Q4 volume +24% and revenue +21%; FY26 volume +15% and revenue +12%. Material margin about 55% in Q4 and 54% for FY26.

guidance_outlook: Food volume growth targeted at mid-teens (double digit) in FY27; top line prioritised over margins through FY27 and possibly part of FY28.
Food to stay EBITDA neutral until FY27; INR 1,500-2,000/ton EBITDA targeted from FY28, subject to scale of ~1.5-1.6 MMT food volume (FY26 about 1.2 MMT).
Steady-state EBITDA per ton guided at about INR 3,500-3,600 (safer end INR 3,500).
Q1 FY27 expected to absorb cost inflation from packaging, chemicals, coal and crude-linked inputs; price corrections planned toward end-April.
Management expects May and June demand to recover; Q1 described as good overall despite weak April. Edible oil and foods growth stated as single-digit, not double-digit, for Q1 per Q&A.
Indonesia B50 biodiesel plan from H2 2026 may firm palm prices and narrow spreads versus soft oils, seen as positive for AWL.
capex_capacity: Krishnapatnam oleo-chemical installation expected by early Q4 FY27 to add Industry Essentials volume.
Food volume at ~1.2 MMT in FY26; management hopes to exceed 1.5-1.6 MMT in FY27 to start consolidating food margins.
Direct outlet reach about 970,000; direct plus indirect reach 2.6 million (Nielsen), against a universe of more than 4 million outlets.
demand_pricing: Edible oil complex rose about 10% in March 2026 on the Iran conflict; sunflower above $1,400/t, soya near $1,300/t, palm $1,220-1,250/t. Industry passed this on to consumers in mid-to-late March.
Packaging is about 2-3% of cost; a 10-15% rise implies roughly 25-50 bps margin impact per quarter. Price correction planned for end-April.
Management estimates demand falls about 1% for every INR 10 rise in oil prices.
Alternate channel grew 43% YoY in Q4 (about 15% of edible oil volume, about 25% of food volume); HoReCa +64%; branded exports +48%; masstige brands +18% volume; Kohinoor +39%.
Alternate channel margin estimated only 50-60 bps above general trade; overall company EBITDA margin around 1.5-2%.
Wheat flour competition from smaller private-label players in FY26 as wheat prices were range-bound; wheat firming could help organised players.
Rupee depreciation in March and elevated freight/vessel availability cited as headwinds for imports and exports.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company gain or lose from the Iran crisis (gas/LPG disruption to HoReCa, edible oil inflation, convenience food upstocking)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 impact was limited because March trade stocking offset price effects; LPG-driven demand destruction was brief, but April demand was sluggish as stocked inventory was consumed.

qa_highlights.question: Food margin sustainability after restructuring and whether FY26 is a new base?
qa_highlights.answer: Food profitability depends on top-line opportunity; priority is volume through FY27, with current margin levels maintained and possibly more aggressive pricing.

qa_highlights.question: Food volume and margin trade-off, and AOP base case?
qa_highlights.answer: Base case is double-digit, mid-teens food volume growth in FY27; margins may be slightly lower (versus about 3% margin in FY26) if opportunities arise, with wheat flour as the key upside.

qa_highlights.question: Steady-state EBITDA per ton and sensitivity to oil price moves?
qa_highlights.answer: Steady state about INR 3,500-3,600/ton. Demand slows about 1% per INR 10 price increase; inventory is managed against international prices and season.

qa_highlights.question: Palm oil plantation plans and Indonesian B50 impact?
qa_highlights.answer: No plans for plantations; Wilmar parent holds palm plantations. B50 from H2 2026 may lift palm prices and narrow spreads, positive for soft-oil-focused AWL.

qa_highlights.question: Why guide margin per ton rather than percentage, and why is valuation low versus peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Per-ton guidance reflects that brand pricing passes through commodity moves, so percentage margins fall while per-ton margins hold. Management said valuation is market-driven and classed the company as food FMCG (70% of revenue from brands).

risks_watch: Q1 FY27 margin pressure from packaging, chemical, coal and crude-linked cost inflation following the Iran conflict.
Weak April demand; recovery in May-June is needed for Q1 to hold up.
Food volume-over-margin strategy may compress food margins against a targeted INR 1,500-2,000/ton from FY28.
Edible oil price volatility and demand elasticity (about 1% per INR 10 move); palm and B50 policy effects.
Interim CFO in place; trade credit versus borrowings shifts and rupee depreciation affect working capital and import costs.
Standalone food volume de-grew in FY26 and the wheat/rice competitive environment remains open.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the Q4 volume, revenue and per-ton metrics, but cautious on Q1 FY27 because of input cost inflation and weak April demand. Management was evasive on specific pricing pass-through and the margin split by product, and deferred valuation questions to the market.
key_quotes: So what we see today is all the elevated price of edible oil complex, which we have not seen at least in last year.
But I'm very sure that in the month of May and June, it will recover, and we will have a fairly good quarter Q1 as well.
we will certainly give priority to the top line rather than margins.

adds.what: Krishnapatnam oleo-chemical installation adding Industry Essentials volume

growth.why: Management targets mid-teens (double-digit) Food volume growth in FY27 and steady-state EBITDA of INR 3,500-3,600/t, backed partly by the Krishnapatnam oleo-chemical plant due by early Q4 FY27 and share gains, but no specific food capacity numbers were given for FY27 and Q1 edible oil and food growth is guided single-digit.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Packaging, chemical, coal and crude-linked inputs are rising after the Iran conflict, with a 10-15% packaging rise worth roughly 25-50 bps of margin per quarter, and Food is guided EBITDA-neutral through FY27 while top line is prioritised; the FY28 food target of INR 1,500-2,000/t is outside this window.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: The Krishnapatnam oleo-chemical installation is expected by early Q4 FY27 to add Industry Essentials volume, though it is a minor addition with no capacity size or capex disclosed.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.when: next 2-4 quarters, with FY27 mid-teens Food growth as the ba
rows.why: Management targets mid-teens (double-digit) Food volume growth in FY27 from ~1.2 MMT, but Q1 FY27 edible oil and food growth is guided single-digit, April demand was sluggish, and demand falls about 1% for every INR 10 rise in oil prices.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Q1 FY27 growth is guided single-digit and cost inflation is flagged for Q1, so no upgrade is signalled in the window despite the record Q4 (volume +14%, EBITDA +40% YoY).

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Weak April demand, cost inflation hitting Q1 rather than Q4, and single-digit Q1 growth against a record Q4 mean Q1 could fall short unless May-June recovers as management expects.

rows.label: Price correction toward end-April to pass through input inflation
rows.why: Management planned price corrections toward end-April to offset packaging, chemical, coal and crude-linked cost rises, though pass-through extent was not quantified and management was evasive on it.

rows.label: Indonesia B50 biodiesel policy lifting palm prices
rows.why: B50 from H2 2026 may firm palm prices and narrow spreads versus soft oils, which management sees as positive for soft-oil-focused AWL, but the effect is conditional on policy.

rows.label: Alternate channel and HoReCa momentum
rows.why: Alternate channel grew 43% YoY in Q4 (about 15% of edible oil volume and 25% of food volume) and HoReCa rose 64%, though channel margin is only 50-60 bps above general trade.

tone.note: Management was confident on Q4 volume (+14%), EBITDA (+40%) and per-ton metrics and on FY27 double-digit food growth, but cautious on Q1 FY27 because of input cost inflation and weak April demand; analysts probed pricing pass-through and the food margin trade-off, which management answered evasively
